quarterly_data.quarter: Accretech (Tokyo Seimitsu) results briefing Q&A: FY2027/3 1Q Earnings Conference Q&A Summary (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): Semiconductor Production Equipment (SPE) orders for the April-June quarter significantly exceeded expectations. Inquiries related to HPC including generative AI were strong, with demand for logic devices, particularly high-end products in China, robust. The company believes the probing market is improving across most applications except certain power discrete devices - demand for analog devices and PMICs for data centers is strong and appears fairly sustainable, and inquiries for DDICs and other products are increasing. Dicer orders were better than expected, with demand not only for capacity expansion but also for new applications such as silicon photonics.

quarterly_data.quarter: Accretech (Tokyo Seimitsu) results briefing Q&A: FY2027/3 1Q Earnings Conference Q&A Summary (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): HPC-related (including generative AI) SPE orders for the April-June quarter were approximately JPY 20.0B, three quarters for logic and one quarter for HBM. HPC-related sales in the same quarter were approximately mid-40% of overall SPE sales, two thirds for logic and one third for HBM.
quarterly_data.figure: HPC orders approximately JPY 20.0B (3/4 logic, 1/4 HBM); HPC sales approximately mid-40% of SPE sales (2/3 logic, 1/3 HBM)

quarterly_data.quarter: Accretech (Tokyo Seimitsu) results briefing Q&A: FY2027/3 1Q Earnings Conference Q&A Summary (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): SPE orders for July-September were guided to decline from April-June partly because April-June appears to have included projects brought forward (no specific figure); at this point the company also anticipates July-September orders could be on par with April-June because it expects HBM-related orders to increase in that quarter. The lower projected HBM order growth for the FY2027/3 first half reflects the expectation that projects originally anticipated for the first half may shift to the second half (or July-September); no specific negative events have occurred.

quarterly_data.quarter: Accretech (Tokyo Seimitsu) results briefing Q&A: FY2027/3 1Q Earnings Conference Q&A Summary (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the order environment is very strong, with orders amounting to about 1.5 times the company's production capacity. Lead times, depending on specifications, are approximately 4-8 months for probers, similar for dicers, and grinder lead times have continued to exceed 6 months.
quarterly_data.figure: orders about 1.5 times production capacity; prober lead times approximately 4-8 months; grinder lead times over 6 months

quarterly_data.quarter: Accretech (Tokyo Seimitsu) results briefing Q&A: FY2027/3 1Q Earnings Conference Q&A Summary (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on the upward capex revision for FY2027/3: to expand prober production the company will move components stored at its main Hanno Plant (Hanno City, Saitama Prefecture) to an external warehouse and convert the space to production (utility modification costs included in the plan; expected to be completed within the current fiscal year), and has assigned approximately 100 employees from within the company to support production. These actions are expected to raise capacity to approximately 1.2 times the current level by the beginning of FY2028/3. Separately, the company is moving forward with a new plant near the Hanno Plant (capital budget added) that will increase production floor space in the Hanno region by 1.5 times, and it is finalizing plans to build a new plant in Hachioji, Tokyo, targeting FY2031/3.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity approximately 1.2 times current level by the beginning of FY2028/3; Hanno-region production space 1.5 times; approximately 100 employees reassigned; Hachioji plant targeting FY2031/3

quarterly_data.quarter: Accretech (Tokyo Seimitsu) results briefing Q&A: FY2027/3 1Q Earnings Conference Q&A Summary (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on the upward revision of the FY2027/3 full-year forecast: no significant changes to the assumptions; margins are expected to improve from higher sales of probers with high-precision temperature control, a shift in grinder sales from PG (Polish Grinder)-based products to the higher-value-added HRG (High Rigid Grinder), and higher dicer sales volumes. The forecast includes the costs of the Hanno Plant capital investment and rising labor costs; as the full amount of planned expenses is factored in, actual results may differ from the forecast. The new forecast assumes a full-year OP margin of 25-6% for the SPE segment.
quarterly_data.figure: SPE segment full-year OP margin assumption 25-6%

quarterly_data.quarter: Accretech (Tokyo Seimitsu) results briefing Q&A: FY2027/3 1Q Earnings Conference Q&A Summary (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): risks to revenue growth include component procurement as well as personnel and production space. The revised revenue forecast includes only projects for which procurement of the components needed for production has been confirmed; if additional components can be secured, production capacity would support revenue several billion yen higher. Management believes the market is certain to expand over the long term.

quarterly_data.quarter: Accretech (Tokyo Seimitsu) results briefing Q&A: FY2027/3 1Q Earnings Conference Q&A Summary (08-04-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on Hybrid Bonding grinders: no significant change from the May briefing outlook - for NAND applications the company expects orders for mass-production equipment starting in the FY2027/3 second half, with shipments expected to begin in the FY2028/3 second half and beyond. Evaluation units have been shipped to target customers and the company expects some to meet customer purchase criteria in FY2027/3, resulting in recognized revenue. The Nagoya Plant, established to strengthen production of Hybrid Bonding grinders, is currently dedicated to grinders for AI packaging; the company is proceeding with capital investment and personnel expansion to move it to full-scale production.
